newsitem.title: USA: Minn. speaker urges governor to sign school biil.
newsitem.headline: Minn. speaker urges governor to sign school biil.

text.p: Minnesota House Speaker Phil Carruthers urged Gov. Arne Carlson on Friday to sign a $6.7 billion education funding bill, contending failure to adopt a full budget by July 1 could jeopardize state efforts to obtain a top bond rating, a spokesman said.
The governor and lawmakers have reached an impasse on the elementary and secondary education package, which did not include $150 million of credits proposed by the governor.
Lawmakers forwarded the spending bill to Carlson Friday afternoon, leaving him three days to decide whether to veto the package, House leadership spokesman Tom Smalec said.

Carlson, a Republican, intends to veto the bill and call a special session for lawmakers to reconsider his proposals to allow credits for private school tuitions, tutors, computers for school use and other education-related expenses, spokesman Brian Dietz said.
A veto of the bill would likely prevent Minnesota from achieving restoration of the top AAA bond rating, Carruthers, Democrat of Brooklyn Center, said in a letter to the governor.
"If you veto the education finance bill, the state could begin the new biennium without a complete budget package," Carruthers wrote. Minnesota sets its budget on a two-year basis.
"Bond rating agencies, to say nothing of average taxpayers, will no doubt be concerned that Minnesota does not have its fiscal house in order," he said.

Failure to resolve the issue by the start of the fiscal biennium on July 1 would also wipe out $800 million of property tax cuts, including a $500 million one-time rebate, approved this session, Carruthers said.
Dietz said, however, that lawmakers would have plenty of time to resolve the differences before the end of the fiscal year.
